full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Gholam Rabbani, J:- Rule is directed against an order dated 11.8.91 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bhanga in Title suit No. 35 of 1986 rejecting the defendant-petitioners, prayer for staying the further proceeding of the suit pending disposal of Civil Revision No.828 of 1991 pending in the High Court Division. 

 2. By the impugned order the learned Assistant Judge directed the petitioner to bring stay order from the High Court Division granting a short time and as such in fact the petitioners, prayer for staying further proceeding of the suit was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge. 

 The petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title suit No. 140 of 1981 in the First Court of Assistant Judge, Bhanga, for declaration of their title in respect of certain lands. The suit was decreed in part by the judgment and decree dated 29.9.83 and against thereof the petitioners preferred Title Appeal No. 58 of 1984 in the Court of District Judge, Faridpur. In that appeal the opposite parties in this Civil Revision filed an application for adding themselves as respondents. Their application was rejected on the ground that they could have filed a separate suit. Thereafter the opposite parties filed the aforesaid Title suit No. 35 of 1989for declaration that the decree passed in Title suit No 140 of 1981 was illegal, fraudulent and not binding upon them. The suit is now pending. Subsequently the learned District Judge dismissed the Title Appeal No. 58 of 1984 as well as dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 20.11.90 and against whereof the petitioner obtained Rule in civil Revision No. 828 of 1991 which is still pending in this Court. The petitioners then filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure in Title suit No.35 of 1989 for staying the further proceeding of the suit till the disposal of the civil Revision by the High Court Division. The learned Assistant Judge by the impugned order dated 11.8.91 apparently rejected the prayer as the Assistant Judge directed the petitioners to bring stay order from the High Court Division. 

 4. Mr. Robindra Gosh, the learned advocate for the petitioners, submits that this Title suit No. 35 of 1989 has been filed for declaration that the decree passed in Title suit No. 140 of 1981 is illegal, fraudulent and not -binding upon the plaintiffs. But as the said decree has already been set aside by the learned District Judge on appeal the suit can only be proceeded with if the High Court Division decreed the suit in Civil Revision No. 828 of 1991 and if the Rule is discharged the suit will become infructuous and unnecessary. The learned advocate, therefore, further submits that the learned Assistant Judge in view of this circumstance ought to have stayed the further proceeding of the suit as prayed for. 

 5. It is well-settled that application for staying a suit normally should be made to the court which has scission of the suit and that where section 10 of the Code of Civil procedure does not strictly apply for the ends of justice suit my be stayed under section 151 of the Code. 

 6. It appears that at the moment there is no existence of the decree which the opposite parties as plaintiffs want to be declared as-illegal, fraudulent and not binding upon them in their Title suit No. 35 of 1989. They can only proceed with the suit if the suit is decreed partly or wholly by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 828 of 1991. I, therefore, find that the learned Assistant Judge ought to have stayed the further proceeding of Title suit No. 35 of 1989 till the disposal of the Civil Revision No. 828 of 1991 and as such the learned Assistant Judge committed error of law resulting error in the impugned order occasioning failure of justice. 

 7. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. It is ordered that the further proceedings of Title suit No. 35 of 1989 pending in the court of the Assistant Judge, Bhanga, will remain stayed till the disposal of Civil Revision No. 828 of 1991 by the High Court Division.
